principle: Prominence is measured as recognisability at social-feed / mobile size, not as raw pixel dimensions. Every rule below is evaluated on the render scaled to a 240px-wide feed proxy (and the 281px thumbnail the 3M pipeline already produces), then reported in canvas pixels for the designer.

feed_proxy.note: ≈ a phone feed card at 1× density; the strictest common case

advantage_bid_led.clear_space: ≥ 1 × logo cap height on all sides
advantage_bid_led.position: logo in the top 22% of the canvas; wordmark in the band
advantage_bid_led.recognition_test: at the feed proxy the logo lockup is identifiable as the Advantage.Bid mark (template match ≥ 0.85) and the wordmark OCRs correctly
advantage_bid_led.first_glance_zone: logo or wordmark must sit inside the top-third or bottom-band zones the eye scans first; never mid-cluster
advantage_bid_led.note: The six proving-ground renders used a 250px lockup (23% of width) — the Owner called it too small in every case. 30–40% is the corrected band; the calibration extreme uses 44%.

seller_led_cobranded.seller_identity: largest identity element; may be type when no seller logo asset exists in production (never lifted from a reference)
seller_led_cobranded.identity_weight: cap-height × width × contrast of the element, normalised; the Advantage.Bid lockup + relationship line together must reach 60–90% of the seller identity's weight — intentionally visible, never competing
seller_led_cobranded.footer_band_wordmark: as advantage_bid_led (the band is the platform's, not the seller's)
never: Advantage.Bid larger than the seller identity
Advantage.Bid identity in the same colour and face as the seller's so the two read as one company
seller_led_cobranded.note: West University A/B/C carried a ~20px relationship line without the logo mark; the band wordmark alone did not satisfy the Owner.

qa.fail: any check → prominence violation → REGENERATE with the identity block enlarged one step (never by shrinking the headline first)
qa.report: canvas px, feed-proxy px, weight ratio, zone

event_type.principle: The viewer must understand WHAT the event is within the first glance. Event Type is a first-class text role.

roles_order_of_visual_weight.note: Order is comprehension order, not size order: SELLER may be smaller than EVENT_TYPE; what must hold is that EVENT_TYPE is never below DATE_TIME in size and never reads as a subtitle.

sizing.modifiers: qualifiers such as 'Exclusive', 'On-Site', 'Two-Day' are modifiers, set at ≤ 45% of the event type's cap height or moved to the support line; they never dilute the type
title_unit_patterns: TYPE_LED: 'Estate Sale' largest; place/name second line at 60–100% of it (the published West University graphic and the Owner's ask)
UNIT: place + type as one unit at equal size ('Katy Estate Sale'; 'West University Estate Sale') — allowed when it fits on ≤ 2 lines without orphaning
TWO_LINE_UNIT: place line / type line, type ≥ 80% of the place line ('Pine Haven' / 'Estate Sale')
forbidden: event type as a sentence-case subtitle under a place-name title (West University A/B/C)
event type wrapped so a word stands alone ('… Estate / Sale')

vocabulary.source: production event record (event_mode + sale_type); never invented; if the record has no type the creative uses the record's title only and the packet flags it

qa.comprehension_test: vision judge at feed proxy: 'What kind of event is this?' must answer with the event type; 'Who is running it?' must answer the seller (co-brand) or Advantage.Bid; 'When?' the date
checks: event_type role present in drawn text
qa.fail: REGENERATE with the title unit re-set

text_hygiene.no_orphan_words: no headline or event-type line may wrap leaving a single word on its own line
text_hygiene.accent_rule_placement: a decorative rule (red underline) sits under the whole headline unit, never under a fragment of one word
